title: Strong connectivity of directed graphs

problem.name: Strong connectivity of directed graphs
problem.statement_latex:
For a directed graph $G=(V,E)$, decide whether every ordered pair $(u,v)$ is joined by a directed path. A constructive version returns the strongly connected components. Applications include reachability and recurrent states in transition systems.
The comparison counts adjacency queries, with classical RAM time stated for explicit adjacency lists.
problem.statement_text: For a directed graph $G=(V,E)$, decide whether every ordered pair $(u,v)$ is joined by a directed path. A constructive version returns the strongly connected components. Applications include reachability and recurrent states in transition systems. The comparison counts adjacency queries, with classical RAM time stated for explicit adjacency lists.

quantum.headline_latex: $\Theta(n^{3/2})$ matrix queries and $O(\sqrt{nm}\log n)$ array queries, quantum directed graph exploration.
quantum.details_latex: The array bound has lower bound $\Omega(\sqrt{nm})$. Classical discovery orders and component records support the quantum searches, and the output can list the strongly connected components. The graph representation supplies outgoing neighbors; this access model determines the array bound.

classical.headline_latex: $O(n+m)$ time, Tarjan or Kosaraju; $\Theta(n^2)$ matrix queries.
classical.details_latex: Tarjan uses depth-first discovery indices and low-link information, while Kosaraju uses two directed traversals. Both produce an explicit component partition. With matrix input, deciding whether a hidden arc closes a one-way cut gives the quadratic classical query requirement.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial, from Grover search and quantum minimum finding. The dense matrix improvement is a factor $\sqrt n$.

evidence.description_latex: Rigorous oracle advantage. The matrix bound is tight, and the array bound is tight up to logarithmic factors.

hardware.description_latex: Fault-tolerant search uses logarithmic vertex-address registers and oracle workspace, with $O(n\log n)$ classical component data. The resource requirement is dominated by repeated coherent access to the directed graph.
